name: Do Not Disturb access
plain: Lets the app read and change Do Not Disturb settings.
meaning: Reveals whether the user is in a focus mode and lets apps toggle it. iOS shows only a yes or no focus status.

android.prompt_ui: Settings toggle: Do Not Disturb access
android.revocation: Settings > Special app access > Do Not Disturb access

ios.note: Returns only a boolean isFocused; cannot change Focus.

limits.headline: Can check and change Do Not Disturb on Android; iPhone shows only a yes or no
limits.user_action: You switch on Do Not Disturb access in Settings (Android), or tap Share Focus Status (iPhone)
can: Check whether Do Not Disturb is on
Change the interruption filter on Android
Learn whether a Focus is on, as a yes or no (iPhone)
cannot: Learn the Focus name or schedule on iPhone
Change Do Not Disturb on Android without the Settings switch
limits.differs: Android lets an allowed app change Do Not Disturb; iPhone gives apps only a yes or no and no control.

story.what_it_is: Lets an app read and change your Do Not Disturb settings.
story.for_you: A special switch asks to let the app control Do Not Disturb. If you allow it, a meeting app can silence your phone for you. A bedtime app can turn it on at night.
story.for_makers: Apps that care about sleep, meetings and focus want to flip the setting for you. Reading it also tells them if you are busy. On iPhone it is only a yes or no.

use_cases.example: A calendar app turns on Do Not Disturb during your meetings.
A sleep app silences notifications at bedtime and turns them back on in the morning.
A workout app silences calls so a run is not interrupted.
A study timer blocks alerts during a study session.
A driving app turns on Do Not Disturb while you drive.
A parent app sets quiet time at school.
A game silences notifications during a match.

story.android_note: Android needs special access to change the interruption filter.
story.ios_note: iPhone only returns a yes or no for whether a Focus is on and cannot change it.
